title: MaskGCT: Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech with Masked Generative Codec Transformer

contributions.purpose: Build a zero-shot TTS system that avoids AR systems' poor robustness/duration control and NAR systems' need for explicit text-speech alignment supervision and phone-level duration prediction
contributions.mechanism: MaskGCT: a fully non-autoregressive two-stage masked generative codec transformer trained with mask-and-predict. Stage 1 text-to-semantic (T2S) predicts masked semantic tokens via in-context learning (text + prompt semantic tokens as prefix, no duration prediction); stage 2 semantic-to-acoustic (S2A) predicts masked acoustic tokens from an RVQ codec; inference generates tokens of specified length in parallel with few iterative steps
contributions.evaluation: Trained on 100K hours of in-the-wild speech; on LibriSpeech, SeedTTS test-en, SeedTTS test-zh outperforms current SOTA zero-shot TTS in quality, similarity, intelligibility. Human-level similarity: SIM-O +0.017/-0.002/+0.027 and SMOS +0.28/+0.32/+0.25 across the three benchmarks; CMOS comparable-or-better than ground truth; comparable WER
contributions.source_quote: we introduce Masked Generative Codec Transformer (MaskGCT), a fully non-autoregressive TTS model that eliminates the need for explicit alignment information between text and speech supervision, as well as phone-level duration prediction.

contributions.purpose: Obtain higher-quality discrete semantic representations of speech than the common k-means approach
contributions.mechanism: Train a VQ-VAE to quantize speech self-supervised-learning (SSL) embeddings instead of using k-means, minimizing information loss even with a single codebook
contributions.evaluation: Qualitative/architectural; enables the single-codebook semantic tokens used by the T2S stage (ablations in appendix)
contributions.source_quote: we train a VQ-VAE [20] to quantize speech self-supervised learning embedding, rather than using k-means to extract semantic tokens that is common in previous work. This approach minimizes the information loss of semantic features even with a single codebook.

contributions.purpose: Show the model generalizes beyond zero-shot TTS as a foundational speech-generation model
contributions.mechanism: Apply MaskGCT via zero-shot or post-training to speech translation (cross-lingual dubbing), voice conversion, emotion control, and speech content editing
contributions.evaluation: Demonstrated across the additional tasks (qualitative scalability study); code and model checkpoints released in Amphion
contributions.source_quote: We investigate the scalability of our system across various tasks, including cross-lingual dubbing, voice conversion, emotion control, and speech content editing, utilizing zero-shot learning or post-training methods. This showcases the potential of our system as a foundational model for speech generation.

self_declared_provenance.quote: SoundStorm [19] was the first attempt to use a masked generative transformer to predict multi-layer acoustic tokens extracted from SoundStream, conditioned on speech semantic tokens; however, it needs to receive the semantic tokens of an AR model as input.

NaturalSpeech 3 [8] decomposes speech into discrete token sequences representing different attributes through special designs and generates tokens ... through masked generative models. However, it still needs speech-text alignment supervision and phone-level duration prediction.
MaskGIT [11] is the first work to use masked generative models for both unconditional and conditional image generation.

notes: Reported accept. Positioned as improving on prior masked-generative TTS: unlike SoundStorm (needs AR-model semantic tokens) and NaturalSpeech 3 (needs alignment + phone-level duration), MaskGCT removes both requirements. Results are largely positive; one mildly negative/comparable figure: SIM-O is -0.002 on SeedTTS test-en (slightly below reference on that benchmark while positive on the other two). Authors acknowledge concurrent alignment-free NAR works (SimpleSpeech, DiTTo-TTS, E2 TTS). Resource released: code + model checkpoints (Amphion), audio samples site.
